- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.4) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — adjust downward bias to match recent low trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true high if sentiment was neutral or bearish.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above true mean, reduce next forecast by 5–10%.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is high 3–5 days after a sentiment spike, reduce by 5–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle — reduce first 5–7 forecast values if sentiment is rising.
